annotations.title: Send the events a webhook missed

description: Send the events your webhook missed while we had it switched off. Turning it back on sends only new events, so this is the only way to get the rest. It sends the events written while it was off that are still in the feed (24 hours) and that no delivery was ever made for, of the types the endpoint subscribes to now: if you changed the types since, those are the ones that count. `catchUp.missed` in `get_webhook` says how many. One call queues up to 1000, oldest first: call it again for the rest. A second call never queues an event twice. The endpoint must be switched on (409 otherwise). A workspace can make 60 resends an hour, and each call counts as one. The answer is how many were queued. A signed-in owner can call this, or an API key with both setup and read permission. A key works only on a webhook a key saved: one a person saved answers 409 `webhookSavedByPerson`, so ask the owner with `create_handoff`, kind `manage_webhook`.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: resend_missed_webhook_events
title: Send the events a webhook missed
